summary: Supplementary tables 3, 4, 10 and 11 report Gough Island versus WSB log2 fold changes for 490 selected hypothalamus genes. Of 431 paired genes, 429 agree in direction (Pearson r = 0.9895 and Spearman rho = 0.9773). Selected-reference coverage is 87.96%, below the 90% required by author-concordance-v2.

manualReview.summary: Compared 431 selected hypothalamus gene effects with the registered Gough Island versus WSB contrast
manualReview.note: Zenodo's preservation copy matches Dryad's file digests. The 490 genes belong to author-selected pathways or QTL sets. 431 have a paired registered coefficient and 429 agree in direction. Both numerical agreement routes meet their thresholds, but 87.96% of the selected reference has a pair. Gene-level author P values and adjusted P values remain unassessed. Both measure the island-minus-WSB difference across sexes in four-week whole hypothalamus. The paper averages sex-specific log2 contrasts from a strain-by-sex model. The registered additive model estimates a common strain effect adjusted for sex in the balanced cohort. Positive values indicate higher expression in Gough mice throughout.
reviewFlags: Only 87.96% of selected author genes have a one-to-one registered coefficient. The policy requires 90%.
The public lists report selected DE genes and omit numeric gene-level P and FDR.
The author and registered fits treat sex differently. Litter effects remain inseparable in the registered model.

verificationReview.nextStep: For full-universe review, obtain the complete four-week hypothalamus sex-averaged strain results with Ensembl IDs, log2 fold changes, raw P and BH-adjusted P including missing values, and reconcile the two model contrasts.

comparabilityReview.basis: Current registered whole-hypothalamus edgeR-QL table, with DE and input identities checked against its serialization-successor provenance.
comparabilityReview.reference: Four-week hypothalamus rows from Nolte et al. supplementary tables 3 and 4 (enriched GO and KEGG terms), 10 (QTL-proximal DE genes) and 11 (QTL/SNP candidates). Article Table 2 repeats rounded entries from supplementary table 10.

cohort.note: The paper sampled four-week-old mouse hypothalamus from both strains and treated each mouse as a replicate. All 20 registered GSMs, tissue, age, sex, strain and animal labels reconcile to GEO, with five mice of each sex per strain. The coefficient lists omit GSMs. The paper describes related litters, including one litter for the four-week island males.

contrast.note: Both measure the island-minus-WSB difference across sexes in four-week whole hypothalamus. The paper averages sex-specific log2 contrasts from a strain-by-sex model. The registered additive model estimates a common strain effect adjusted for sex in the balanced cohort. Positive values indicate higher expression in Gough mice throughout.

features.note: Deduplicated GO, KEGG and QTL entries by mouse Ensembl gene ID. Each of the 431 pairs links to a unique identical input and canonical count profile across all GSMs and an author or MGI symbol corroborates the published symbol. The row audit accounts for every remaining ID, including Eno1, whose registered count profile differs from the individual author feature.

effects.note: Sex-averaged DESeq2 and common edgeR strain effects have compatible direction and log2 units. Pearson r = 0.9895 and Spearman rho = 0.9773. 429/431 nonzero pairs agree in sign. Median absolute log2 difference is 0.0237. Effects differ in sign for Lsm8, Selenbp2. The model and normalization differences permit different magnitudes.

inference.note: The paper used DESeq2 with a strain-by-sex interaction and selected genes at BH-adjusted P < 0.05 before pathway or QTL selection. Explorer used edgeR quasi-likelihood on length-scaled counts with sex as an additive covariate. Of 431 pairs, 371 meet registered FDR < 0.05. All 3,324 registered discoveries lack numeric author FDR, and 2,953 also lack a paired selected coefficient. Full call-list overlap and finite paired P/FDR agreement remain unassessed.

coverage.note: 431/490 selected author genes (87.96%) and 431/15,568 published genes (2.77%) have paired effects for gough_vs_wsb. The 59 unpaired author IDs remain in the denominator. The public tables do not supply the complete tested-gene universe.

comparabilityReview.criteria: author-concordance-v2 requires at least 30 pairs and 90% relevant coverage. Either Pearson and Spearman must both reach 0.90, or at least 90% of at least 30 nonzero pairs must agree in sign with those pairs covering at least 90% of all pairs. Cohort, contrast, features and effect definitions must also be compatible. Selected scope uses every distinct selected author gene as its denominator.
comparabilityReview.conclusion: Direct comparison is closed for selected genes. The correlation and direction criteria pass on the pairs, but selected-reference coverage is 87.96%. Full author inference and full verification remain open.
